unverified.firing_order: 1-5-4-8-6-3-7-2 per Ford only (1933 V-8 booklet '15486372'; same in the 1953 Ford owner's manual for the 239).
unverified.rod_length_in: 7 in per Ford 1933 V-8 booklet spec table only.
unverified.block_material: Cast iron (Wikipedia: 'Like most other engine blocks of the 20th century, it was cast iron'); Ford literature says only 'one-piece casting of crankcase and cylinder banks'.
unverified.head_material_1932: Cast iron implied by Ford's 1933 booklet presenting aluminum heads as new; EngineLabs says early 1932 engines had aluminum heads. Unresolved.
unverified.compression_ratio: 1932 5.5:1 (Wikipedia, EngineLabs - two agree); 1933-34 6.33:1 (Wikipedia only); 1935-36 6.3:1 (Wikipedia only); 1937-38 6.2:1 aluminum / 7.5:1 iron (Wikipedia, EngineLabs - two agree); late-1938 V8-81A 6.12:1 (Wikipedia only).
